raw_response:
I've been farming this land in Quzhou my whole life. My children went to the city years ago, and my husband is gone, so it's mostly me now, with a neighbor helping at planting and harvest. I'm 68 and my back isn't what it was. I can't manage more than about 5 mu on my own.

I'll grow winter wheat then summer corn on the same 5 mu — that's the rotation my parents did and their parents before them. Everyone in the village does it. The wheat goes in before winter frost, you harvest it in June, then immediately put in the corn. That's how you get two crops from one piece of land. I'll also keep a small half-mu kitchen plot with some vegetables — garlic, cabbage — just for my own household.

For seeds, I'll go to Lao Zhang's shop in the village and buy whatever improved wheat variety he has — he sold me Jimai 22 last year and it did fine. For corn I'll get hybrid seed, same as always, that's all they sell now anyway.

Fertilizer: I'll put down diammonium phosphate at planting like I always do, then topdress with urea in spring for the wheat. For corn I'll do the same. I don't measure exactly — I use the amounts the agricultural station recommended years ago and I've stuck with them.

Water: I'll irrigate the wheat three times — before sowing to wet the soil, at jointing, and at heading. Corn usually gets rain in summer but I'll pump once if it looks dry. The well pump costs money so I don't water more than needed.

I'll spray for pests if I see aphids or armyworm. I won't spray just to spray — that costs money.

For tillage, I'll hire the village rotary tiller — I can't do it myself anymore. For the corn I'll seed directly into the stubble, no second tillage needed.
